dc_eval_persuasion.quote: Fig. 4.2.1.A Upper section: The score for each model, averaged across 414 conversations, on the dimensions
dc_eval_persuasion.description: Bar chart of automated behavioral audit scores (1-10 scale, and count of conversations scored above 5) per model including Claude Opus 4, with a 'Manipulative' dimension defined on p45 as the degree to which the target acts emotionally manipulative toward the auditor; Opus 4 shows a low mean score near 1.1 and a small count.
dc_eval_persuasion.note: Manipulation is listed as a looked-for behaviour in text (current 1); the result for this model on the named automated behavioral audit appears only in Fig 4.2.1.A (clarification 4). Looked at all 49 listed pages (32 card, 17 ASL-3 report); the ASL-3 report has no persuasion content.

safeguards_access.quote: we have developed a verification system to enable controlled access where appropriate. This system offers controlled access to entitles with which we have an established relationship
safeguards_access.note: ASL-3 safety report naming Claude Opus 4 (clarification 9), section 2.2.4 Access controls: vetted trusted-user access with targeted classifier exemptions, tied to the ASL-3 Deployment Standard's trusted-users criterion, i.e. a trusted access programme tied to safety. Card pages and figures add nothing further.
